question.text: Stock brokers must segregate clients' securities and:

answer.text: Not use them for self or for other clients
Use them only with client consent
Pledge them for margin on behalf of the client
Pool them in a common account for efficiency

explanation.text: The Logic: The Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956 and the SEBI (Stock-Brokers) Regulations, 1992 require stock brokers to segregate client securities or moneys and not use them for self or for other clients. The Trap: 'Use with client consent' sounds reasonable but the rule on the controlling page is stated as a no-use requirement; the workbook page checked does not establish a general consent-based carve-out. Note: The Series VI workbook (p.167) is the controlling source for the segregation/no-use rule. Pages on DDPI and pledge workflows describe separate operational mechanisms and do not create an exception for using client securities or moneys for self or other clients.
